18754-ohio-biological-survey-bull-10-vol.title: Ohio Biological Survey Bull 10 Vol 11 No 6 The Ascomycetes O
18754-ohio-biological-survey-bull-10-vol.creator: Bruce Fink
18754-ohio-biological-survey-bull-10-vol.description: A book by Bruce Fink. In structure, the thallus is crustose, and the thalli vary from inconspicuous, evanescent conditions to those which are conspicuous and sometimes even subsquamulous. Rarely the thallus extends upward as a veil which surrounds the apothecia laterally and suggests how the thalloid exciple of higher families probably arose.

arxiv-2105-12091.title: Fundamental limitations in Lindblad descriptions of systems weakly coupled to baths
arxiv-2105-12091.creator: Devashish Tupkary, Abhishek Dhar, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha
arxiv-2105-12091.description: Abstract It is very common in the literature to write down a Markovian quantum master equation in Lindblad form to describe a system with multiple degrees of freedom and weakly connected to multiple thermal baths which can, in general, be at different temperatures and chemical potentials.

arxiv-2205-12302.title: Garden Path Traversal in GPT-2
arxiv-2205-12302.creator: William Jurayj, William Rudman, Carsten Eickhoff
arxiv-2205-12302.description: Abstract In recent years, large-scale transformer decoders such as the GPT-x family of models have become increasingly popular. Studies examining the behavior of these models tend to focus only on the output of the language modeling head and avoid analysis of the internal states of the transformer decoder.

arxiv-2207-06392.title: Relationship Design for Socially-Aware Behavior in Static Games
arxiv-2207-06392.creator: Shenghui Chen, Yigit E. Bayiz, David Fridovich-Keil, Ufuk Topcu
arxiv-2207-06392.description: Abstract Autonomous agents can adopt socially-aware behaviors to reduce social costs, mimicking the way animals interact in nature and humans in society. We present a new approach to model socially-aware decision-making that includes two key elements: bounded rationality and inter-agent relationships.

arxiv-2210-12344.title: Systematic KMTNet Planetary Anomaly Search, Paper VII: Complete Sample of q < 10 − 4 q<10^{-4} Planets from the First Four-Year Survey
arxiv-2210-12344.creator: Weicheng Zang, Youn Kil Jung, Hongjing Yang, Xiangyu Zhang, Andrzej Udalski, Jennifer C. Yee, Andrew Gould, Shude Mao, Michael D. Albrow, Sun-Ju Chung, Cheongho Han, Kyu-Ha Hwang, Yoon-Hyun Ryu, In-Gu Shin, Yossi Shvartzvald, Sang-Mok Cha, Dong-Jin Kim, Hyoun-Woo Kim, Seung-Lee Kim, Chung-Uk Lee, Do
arxiv-2210-12344.description: Abstract We present the analysis of seven microlensing planetary events with planet/host mass ratios q < 10 − 4 q<10^{-4} : KMT-2017-BLG-1194, KMT-2017-BLG-0428, KMT-2019-BLG-1806, KMT-2017-BLG-1003, KMT-2019-BLG-1367, OGLE-2017-BLG-1806, and KMT-2016-BLG-1105. They were identified by applying the Korea Microlensing Telescope Network (KMTNet) AnomalyFinder algorithm to 2016–2019 KMTNet events.

arxiv-2211-13320.title: The growth of intermediate mass black holes through tidal captures and tidal disruption events 2020 The growth of intermediate mass black holes through tidal captures and tidal disruption events – References
arxiv-2211-13320.creator: Francesco Paolo Rizzuto, Thorsten Naab, Antti Rantala, Peter H. Johansson, Jeremiah P. Ostriker, Nicholas C. Stone, Shihong Liao, Dimitrios Irodotou
arxiv-2211-13320.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Francesco Paolo Rizzuto, Thorsten Naab, Antti Rantala, Peter H. Johansson, Jeremiah P. Ostriker, Nicholas C. Stone, Shihong Liao, Dimitrios Irodotou. We present N − body N\mathrm{-body} simulations, including post-Newtonian dynamics, of dense clusters of low-mass stars harbouring central black holes (BHs) with initial masses of 50, 300, and 2000 M ⊙ \mathrm{M_{\odot}} .

arxiv-2307-07589.creator: Mina Huh, Yi-Hao Peng, Amy Pavel
arxiv-2307-07589.description: Abstract . Blind and low vision (BLV) creators use images to communicate with sighted audiences. However, creating or retrieving images is challenging for BLV creators as it is difficult to use authoring tools or assess image search results. Thus, creators limit the types of images they create or recruit sighted collaborators.

arxiv-2309-06489.title: The q − q- state Potts model from the Nonperturbative Renormalization Group
arxiv-2309-06489.creator: Carlos A. Sánchez-Villalobos, Bertrand Delamotte, Nicolás Wschebor
arxiv-2309-06489.description: Abstract We study the q q -state Potts model for q q and the space dimension d d arbitrary real numbers using the Derivative Expansion of the Nonperturbative Renormalization Group at its leading order, the local potential approximation (LPA and LPA’).

arxiv-2311-02419.title: Deterministic generation of hybrid entangled states using quantum walks
arxiv-2311-02419.creator: Jaskaran Singh, Vikash Mittal, Soumyakanti Bose
arxiv-2311-02419.description: Abstract In recent times, hybrid-entanglement (HE) between a qubit and a coherent state has demonstrated superior performance in various quantum information processing tasks, particularly in quantum key distribution. Despite its theoretical advantages, efficient generation of such states in the laboratory has been a challenge. Here, we introduce a deterministic and efficient approach for generating HE states using quantum walks.

arxiv-2402-09668.title: How to Train Data-Efficient LLMs
arxiv-2402-09668.creator: Noveen Sachdeva, Benjamin Coleman, Wang-Cheng Kang, Jianmo Ni, Lichan Hong, Ed H. Chi, James Caverlee, Julian McAuley, Derek Zhiyuan Cheng
arxiv-2402-09668.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Noveen Sachdeva, Benjamin Coleman, Wang-Cheng Kang, Jianmo Ni, Lichan Hong, Ed H. Chi, James Caverlee, Julian McAuley, Derek Zhiyuan Cheng. The training of large language models (LLMs) is expensive. In this paper, we study data-efficient approaches for pre-training LLMs, i.e. , techniques that aim to optimize the Pareto frontier of model quality and training resource/data consumption.

arxiv-2506-05593.title: Improving Neural Diarization through Speaker Attribute Attractors and Local Dependency Modeling
arxiv-2506-05593.creator: David Palzer, Matthew Maciejewski, Eric Fosler-Lussier
arxiv-2506-05593.description: Abstract In recent years, end-to-end approaches have made notable progress in addressing the challenge of speaker diarization, which involves segmenting and identifying speakers in multi-talker recordings. One such approach, Encoder-Decoder Attractors (EDA), has been proposed to handle variable speaker counts as well as better guide the network during training.

arxiv-2511-02358.title: Let Multimodal Embedders Learn When to Augment Query via Adaptive Query Augmentation DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: the 34th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’25), November 10–14, 2025, Seoul, Republic of Korea; November 10–04, 2025; Seoul, Republic of Kor
arxiv-2511-02358.creator: Wongyu Kim, Hochang Lee, Sanghak Lee, Yoonsung Kim, Jaehyun Park
arxiv-2511-02358.description: Abstract . Query augmentation makes queries more meaningful by appending further information to the queries to find relevant documents. Current studies have proposed Large Language Model (LLM)-based embedders, which learn representation for embedding and generation for query augmentation in a multi-task manner by leveraging the generative capabilities of LLM.

arxiv-2511-11857.title: Three Stage Narrative Analysis; Plot-Sentiment Breakdown, Structure Learning and Concept Detection
arxiv-2511-11857.creator: Taimur Khan and Ramoza Ahsan and Mohib Hameed
arxiv-2511-11857.description: Abstract Story understanding and analysis have been a challenging domain of Natural Language Understanding. The need for automated narrative analysis demands deep computational semantic captures, along with the syntactic analysis of the text. Moreover, a large amount of narrative data requires automated semantic analysis and computational learning rather than manual approaches to the analytical tasks.

arxiv-2605-28721.creator: HuiMing Fan, Xiao Wang, Zheng Chu, Qianyu Wang, Zhuoyao Wang, Ming Liu, Bing Qin, XingYu

pmc-10496701.title: Machine learning models for predicting pre-eclampsia: a systematic review protocol
pmc-10496701.creator: Amene Ranjbar, Elham Taeidi, Vahid Mehrnoush, Nasibeh Roozbeh, Fatemeh Darsareh
pmc-10496701.description: IntroductionPre-eclampsia is one of the most serious clinical problems of pregnancy that contribute significantly to maternal mortality worldwide. This systematic review aims to identify and summarise the predictive factors of pre-eclampsia using machine learning models and evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of machine learning models in predicting pre-eclampsia.

pmc-10585566.title: The evolution and current situation in the application of dual-energy computed tomography: a bibliometric study
pmc-10585566.creator: Ya Wang, Yun Peng, Tongtong Wang, Hui Li, Zhen Zhao, Lianggeng Gong, Bibo Peng
pmc-10585566.description: BackgroundDual-energy computed tomography (DECT) has received extensive attention in clinical practice; however, a quantitative assessment of published literature in this domain is presently lacking. This study thus aimed to characterize the application conditions, developmental trends, and research hot spots of DECT using bibliometric analysis.

pmc-11433309.title: The Mirror Theory: Parallels between Open Angle and Angle Closure Glaucoma
pmc-11433309.creator: Vasile Potop, Christiana Diana Maria Dragosloveanu, Alina Mihaela Ciocâlteu, Miruna Gabriela Burcel, Maria Cristina Marinescu, Dana Margareta Cornelia Dăscălescu, Alba Martín-Gil, Laura De Diego-García, Claudio Iovino, Michele Lanza, Jay Chhablani
pmc-11433309.description: Glaucoma is a widespread ophthalmological disease, with a high impact and frequent visual morbidity. While the physiopathology of the two types of primary glaucoma (open angle and angle closure) has been studied, there seems to be little relationship between the two.

pmc-11453686.title: 7434 Modulation of FGFR-FGF2-FGF23 Signaling Partially Rescues Osteoarthritis in Hyp Mice Homolog of Human X- Linked Hypophosphatemia
pmc-11453686.creator: M M Hurley, L Xiao
pmc-11453686.description: Disclosure: M.M. Hurley: None. L. Xiao: None.Human with X-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH) and its Hyp mice homolog develop several phenotypic abnormalities due to phosphate wasting mediated by abnormal Fibroblast Growth Factor Receptor-1 (FGFR1) and Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF23) signaling. XLH and Hyp mice also develop severe osteoarthropathy (OA) whose etiology is not fully defined.

pmc-11517977.title: Parent perspectives on sports betting and its effects on children
pmc-11517977.creator: A Donaldson, B Cardak, E Seal, E Randle, K Staley, M Nicholson, P O’Halloran
pmc-11517977.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundGambling-related harm is a global challenge. Sports betting is a rapidly growing form of gambling, facilitated by access to online wagering platforms and increased advertising. Most public health initiatives target ‘problem’ gamblers, ignoring socio-cultural influences.

pmc-11640055.title: A Black Sticky Rice-Derived Functional Ingredient Improves Anxiety, Depression, and Stress Perception in Adult Volunteers
pmc-11640055.creator: Pattamaporn Natthee, Jintanaporn Wattanathorn, Wipawee Thukham-mee, Pongsatorn Paholpak, Poonsri Rangseekajee, Nawanant Piyavhatkul, Suphayanakorn Wattanathorn, Supaporn Muchimapura, Terdthai Tong-Un
pmc-11640055.description: We hypothesized that consumption of a diet containing the functional ingredient from black sticky rice, which is rich in anthocyanin, over a five-day period would improve anxiety, depression, and stress perception in adult volunteers based on the benefits of this compound.

pmc-11657077.title: Amelioration of Focal Hand Dystonia via Low‐Frequency Repetitive Somatosensory Stimulation
pmc-11657077.creator: Lorenzo Rocchi, Anna Latorre, Elisa Menozzi, Vittorio Rispoli, John C. Rothwell, Alfredo Berardelli, Kailash P. Bhatia
pmc-11657077.description: BackgroundDystonia presents a growing concern based on evolving prevalence insights. Previous research found that, in cervical dystonia, high‐frequency repetitive somatosensory stimulation (RSS; HF‐RSS) applied on digital nerves paradoxically diminishes sensorimotor inhibitory mechanisms, whereas low‐frequency RSS (LF‐RSS) increases them. However, direct testing on affected body parts was not conducted.

pmc-11728681.title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility Trends in E. coli Causing Pediatric Urinary Tract Infections in the United States
pmc-11728681.creator: Simren Mahajan, Neena Kanwar, Gina M. Morgan, Rodrigo E. Mendes, Brian R. Lee, Dithi Banerjee, Rangaraj Selvarangan
pmc-11728681.description: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are among the most common pediatric infections. This study evaluated the antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of 3511 uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) isolated from pediatric patients in the United States from 2014 to 2023. The database from the SENTRY antimicrobial surveillance program from 89 medical centers was utilized as a data source.

pmc-12741427.title: A promising therapeutic approach for post-Lassa fever sensorineural hearing loss: a case report
pmc-12741427.creator: Sulymon A Saka, Faustina F Blackie, Eustace E Oseghale, Magdalene Akhabule, Okechukwu J Eze, Aiwanose D Ebhota, Joachim O Oboh, Evans Abumen, Monday Agbonifo
pmc-12741427.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic illness endemic in West Africa, with Nigeria accounting for a significant proportion of global cases. While most patients recover, sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) is a serious and often overlooked post-infectious complication. We present the case of a 13-year-old girl who developed sudden profound right-sided SNHL shortly after recovering from Lassa fever, despite a high cycle threshold (Ct) value on PCR, indicating low viral load.

pmc-13038571.title: Case Report: Marchiafava-Bignami disease: anti-parietal cell antibodies as a potential etiological factor in a novel case presentation
pmc-13038571.creator: Junhao Zhang, Lizhen Wang, Shuangfeng Yang, Yinhong Xie, Chengcheng He, Hongyu Lin, Yang Li, Shanfeng Qiu, Shunxian Wang, Shengxiong Pu, Pei Wang, Lei Zhang, Jian Chen, Yang Peng, Yun Liu, Ying Ma
pmc-13038571.description: Marchiafava-Bignami disease (MBD) represents a rare neurological disorder predominantly associated with chronic ethanol consumption and thiamine insufficiency. However, its possible correlation with cobalamin deficiency resulting from anti-parietal cell antibodies (APCA) remained inadequately characterized in the literature. Timely diagnosis and therapeutic intervention were critical for optimizing clinical outcomes.

pmc-13218034.title: Mepiquat chloride enhances cold tolerance in cotton via regulating root growth and antioxidant enzymes
pmc-13218034.creator: Irshad Ahmad, Tianyao Meng, Xuebing Yan, Zhu Guanglong, Muhammad Usama Younas, Guisheng Zhou, Yanqing Wu
pmc-13218034.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Cold stress severely affects cotton growth and yield worldwide. Mepiquat chloride (MC), a widely used plant growth regulator in cotton, has not been extensively studied under cold stress conditions. This study evaluated the effects of three MC levels (0 mM, 50 mM, and 100 mM) applied at 21 days after sowing (DAS) on the morpho-physiological and biochemical responses of two cotton varieties (Sikang 1 and Sikang 3) under normal temperature and cold stress during the seedling stage.

pmc-13430562.title: The Redesign of the Molecular Scaffold of Viral Ion Channel Blockers
pmc-13430562.creator: Balázs Zoltán Zsidó, Erzsébet Mernyák, Zoltán Kopasz, Fanni Földes, Krisztina Leiner, Mónika Madai, Brigitta Zana, Anett Kuczmog, Csaba Hetényi
pmc-13430562.description: The rise of rapidly mutating viruses poses growing challenges for drug developers in the fight against antiviral resistance. Viral ion channels generally have low mutation rates and are therefore considered emerging targets for a sustainable solution to the problem of resistance. This study reports the redesign of scaffolds for drug candidates targeting viral ion channels.

pmc-13440183.title: Burnout and workload among clinical educators in physiotherapy teaching clinics: an observational study
pmc-13440183.creator: Alberto Bermejo-Franco, Daniel Veiga-Pérez, Maxime Quentin Lejeune, Nuria Muñoz-Bermúdez, Ana Mallo-López, José Ángel Del-Blanco-Muñiz
pmc-13440183.description: BackgroundPhysiotherapy clinical educators play a key role in guiding students through practical training, but heavy teaching, managerial, and clinical demands increase their risk of burnout. Understanding the factor’s influencing burnout is essential to support educators’ wellbeing and maintain high-quality clinical education.

pmc-13543897.title: Protocol to improve isoform-level quantification of low-abundance transcripts via STALARD pre-amplification
pmc-13543897.creator: Daesong Jeong, Chulmin Park, Ilha Lee
pmc-13543897.description: SummarySTALARD (selective target amplification for low-abundance RNA detection) enables isoform-level quantification of low-abundance RNAs using conventional laboratory equipment. Here, we describe steps for RNA isolation, primer design, reverse transcription, selective target amplification, and downstream analysis. The protocol couples selective pre-amplification with a quantitative reverse-transcription PCR (RT-qPCR) readout and optional nanopore sequencing.

pmc-13571434.title: Pedicle Screw–Aortic Interaction: A Single Centre Experience and Proposal for a Morphology Based Management Algorithm
pmc-13571434.creator: Federica Campana, Stefano Ancetti, Chiara Cini, Paolo Spath, Alessia Pini, Enrico Gallitto, Alessandro Gasbarrini, Mauro Gargiulo

pmc-13600620.title: Identifying shared polygenic risk across cancers
pmc-13600620.creator: Jiaqi Hu, Maiyier Muheyati, Leqi Xu, Andrew DeWan, Hongyu Zhao, Kent W. Hunter, Heather J Cordell, Kent W. Hunter, Heather J Cordell, Kent W. Hunter, Heather J Cordell
pmc-13600620.description: BackgroundShared genetic susceptibility across cancers has been reported but is generally modest at the genome-wide level. Whether such shared polygenic risk exhibits structured convergence at regional or functional levels remains unclear. We investigated shared genetic risk across cancers by integrating local genetic correlation analyses with cross-cancer polygenic risk score (PRS) associations.

pmc-13650287.title: Microbial profiles and antimicrobial susceptibility in recurrent and non-recurrent canine otitis externa in Brazil
pmc-13650287.creator: Lucas Giordano Ono, Cássia Barros Pimenta, Camila Dorotea Costa, Flavia Simone Munin, Felipe Eguti de Carvalho, Ricardo Luiz Moro de Sousa, Deise Carla Almeida Leite Dellova
pmc-13650287.description: Background and Aim:Canine otitis externa is a common inflammatory disorder in which bacterial and yeast proliferation may complicate treatment and contribute to recurrence. In Brazil, limited information is available comparing recurrent and non-recurrent cases while simultaneously characterizing microbial isolates and their antimicrobial susceptibility.
